answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires cryptographic stake burning scaled superlinearly with identity generation. Each agent ties its verified beacon state to an onyx key registry; registering $n$ identities forces burned collateral to follow a superlinear cost curve $C(n) \propto n^{1.5}$. This economic friction creates a prohibitive financial spiral for coordinated attackers while keeping marginal verification cheap for honest participants.
